subject: Peak-shift capacity coupling & device-matching proposal for HelixAI commit

Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HelixAI expected traffic shape & committed TPS — quick context

Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We got internal approval to move forward with a Reserved Dedicated deployment and want to lock down the capacity assumptions before the commercial review. High level: the product team expects two daily peaks (09:00-11:30 PT and 17:00-19:30 PT) driven by regional business cycles, plus an unpredictable 30–60 minute spike window following release events.

Attached is our synthetic qps profile and sample request traces (helix_qps_profile.csv). Key asks from our side:
- Can Redwood map this to a committed GPU footprint (H100-equivalent) with p95 latency <= 250ms for the Llama-variant model we discussed (seq_len 1024 avg)?
- What headroom percentage would you recommend to cover the two daily peaks + a single 60-minute release spike?
- What fallback plan would you recommend if we hit >150% of committed TPS?

We need a short capacity recommendation pack for procurement by next Thursday. Happy to hop on a call if helpful.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Infrastructure, HelixAI

Subject: Re: HelixAI expected traffic shape & committed TPS — quick context

Samir — thanks for the profile. I skimmed the CSV and confirmed the two-peaks + short unpredictable spikes pattern. Below is our preliminary operational mapping; will follow up with a one-page PDF with precise GPU counts and a short ops playbook.

Summary (first-pass):
- Baseline model: LlamaX-33B q4x (production variant we recommended in demo).
- Average token generation per request: ~420 tokens (mean), avg sequence length ~1024 tokens total processing (prompt + response).
- Measured tokens/sec throughput on our tuned runtime (seq_len 1024, q4x): ~5,200 tokens/sec per H100-80GB instance under continuous batching (p95 latency budget ~220ms at target batching).

Requested answers:
1) Committed GPU footprint: for the 2 daily peaks (peak sustained = 9,800 tokens/sec) + 60-min release spike (peak transient = 18,000 tokens/sec), my rough mapping is: commit to 2x H100-equivalent nodes (each 5,200 tps) yields 10,400 tps sustained. That covers the 2 daily peaks but not the release spike.
2) Headroom: recommend a 40% buffer above committed sustained peak to cover queuing and variable request mix (so commit to ~14,000 tps effective capacity).
3) Fallback: automatic routing to a quantized 13B variant (LlamaX-13B q4f) as burst fallback — adds ~2.6x tokens/sec efficiency and preserves p95 latency (p95 ~260ms) with graceful QoS degradation.

I'll run a quick sensitivity calc with Karthik and Ben (cc'd) and attach a short PDF with the commit suggestion + a 72-hour ops playbook that details warmup/caching and an emergency burst policy.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: quick calc for HelixAI commit (numbers + ops plan)

Team — copying the traffic profile from Samir. Need rapid sanity check and two options for procurement: Conservative commit (higher fixed GPUs, smaller fallback use) and Cost-efficient commit (smaller commit + defined burst SLA). Notes below.

Traffic baseline extracted from helix_qps_profile.csv:
- Two sustained peaks per day: 09:00-11:30 PT and 17:00-19:30 PT. Sustained peak token demand: 9.8k tps.
- Release spike: single hour, transient up to 18k tps.
- Quiet baseline: 1.2k tps overnight.

Performance assumptions (empirical from our infra):
- H100-80GB (tuned runtime, q4x) = 5,200 tokens/sec @ p95 latency 220ms for seq_len 1024, typical prompt mix.
- LlamaX-13B q4f (quantized lighter variant) = 13,000 tokens/sec @ p95 260ms (per H100 equivalent). Efficiency ~2.5x vs 33B.
- Prefix KV cache reduces effective seq_len for repeat traffic by ~18% during morning peak windows. We can count that as seasonal efficiency.

Option A — Conservative (procurement-friendly, higher commit):
- Committed: 3 H100-equivalent GPUs => committed capacity = 15,600 tps (3 * 5,200).
- Suggested headroom: 40% applied to daily peak => target floor capacity = 9.8k * 1.4 = 13.7k tps; 3 GPUs cover this with small cushion.
- Burst plan: allow 60-min spike to 18k tps via short-term burst (auto-burst to cloud pool) + fallback to 13B variant if sustained beyond 60 minutes. Estimated cost uplift for burst pool: +22% of monthly committed cost for 6 burst hours/month.

Option B — Cost-efficient (lower commit, structured burst & fallback):
- Committed: 2 H100-equivalent GPUs => 10.4k tps committed.
- Operational headroom via autoscaler + cache warm-up: aim to cover 12–13k tps effectively during peaks by aggressive KV cache and pre-warming.
- Burst policy: immediate fallback to 13B quantized variant for the first 30 minutes of a spike (expected p95 ~260ms), and automated auto-scale to ephemeral cloud pool if >120% sustained for 10 minutes.
- Estimated monthly saving vs Option A: ~28% on committed fee, but higher burst costs and slightly higher SLA risk.

Quick sensitivity table (back-of-envelope):
- If average seq_len drops to 820 (shorter prompts), H100 throughput increases to ~6,400 tps per GPU — both options improve headroom by ~20%.
- If variance of release spikes grows (multiple hour-long spikes), Option A is safer.

Action items I need from you both:
- Ben: give ops estimate for warm-perf cost to pre-warm caches for 45 minutes prior to expected morning peak and for release flash events. Add expected minutes of warm time per month and cost delta.
- Karthik: draft two line items for procurement showing committed GPU counts, burst SKUs, and estimated monthly committed vs burst spend (include rough token-unit cost translations).

Cc'ing Samir in the wrap once we have numbers.

—Jonas

Subject: Peak-shift capacity recommendation & next steps (HelixAI)

Samir — attaching a short PDF (redwood_peak_shift_proposal.pdf) that summarizes two buy options and an ops playbook. TL;DR below.

TL;DR recommendation (procurement-ready):
- Recommend Option A (Conservative commit): 3x H100-equivalent reserved GPUs. Rationale: covers 9.8k sustained peak + 40% headroom (~13.7k tps) and provides buffer for unexpected multi-hour spikes. This reduces reliance on ephemeral burst and simplifies SLA language for procurement.
- Burst and fallback: 60-minute automatic burst to cloud pool (pre-approved SKU) + automatic fallback to LlamaX-13B q4f for user-facing degraded mode if burst queueing exceeds 90s.
- Ops playbook highlights: staged cache warm-up 45 min pre-peak, release-spike pre-warm trigger via webhook, telemetry thresholds (p95 latency > 260ms for 3 consecutive min => trigger burst).

Deliverables attached: redwood_peak_shift_proposal.pdf (one-pager with GPU counts, cost delta, and rollout steps), ops_playbook.md (72-hour playbook). Also included is a sample DocuSign link for a 12-month committed plan (we can remove if you need monthly).

If that sounds good, I'll push a procurement-ready quote and a DocuSign draft. We can also prepare a scaled Option B if procurement wants smaller upfront commit with higher burst exposure.

Best,
